The curriculum gives students experience with a variety of research methods and theoretical perspectives as they prepare to do their own scholarly work in the field. Students work closely with faculty, and are well-supported in their professional goals, whether they aim to go on to Ph.D. programs in rhetoric or a related field, or to pursue careers in which advanced training in communication and analysis is highly valued. The M.A. in Rhetoric degree requires 72 units of coursework, usually fulfilled by taking three graduate courses per semester for two semesters. A required course, 76-701 Introduction to Rhetorical Theory, is offered in the fall. An M.A. Thesis (76-800) is also required. Other courses are chosen from the graduate seminars regularly offered by rhetoric faculty.
ScholarshipType: Full-tuition remission and teaching assistantship stipend

Department: Dietrich College of Humanities and Social Sciences
Description: The graduate program in Rhetoric at Carnegie Mellon is a Ph.D. program that prepares students for research and teaching in universities and for research in the private and public sectors. We view rhetoric as the study of how language and other symbolic systems are used to create, maintain, and transform our social worlds. We are interested in how people communicate, why they communicate in the particular ways that they do, how they learned to do so, and how their communication might be improved. In exploring these questions we have focused on a wide range of written, oral, and visual texts, from scientific and technical articles to public policy debates, from courtroom arguments to online discussion groups. Research in rhetoric at Carnegie Mellon is problem-driven, eclectic in method, and interdisciplinary. The program takes advantage of the university's strengths in technology, communication, and interdisciplinary research. Further information about the program may be found at the Department of English World Wide Web server.
ScholarshipType: Fellowship, Stipend, Tuition Remission, Health Insurance Subsidy

Department: Dietrich College of Humanities and Social Sciences
Concentration: ['Social and Cultural History', 'Global History', 'History of Science, Technology, and the Environment']
Description:
The graduate program in history at Carnegie Mellon is small, selective, and innovative. We are best known for our interdisciplinary approach to historical studies and our focus on the historical roots of contemporary social, political, and economic problems. Our program is organized into three broad fields of study: Social and Cultural History, Global History, and the History of Science, Technology, and the Environment. Although there are many areas of overlap and connection between these fields, all students will select a major field in one of these three areas and develop two minor fields in consultation with their advisors. Students will also be expected to achieve competence in a foreign language or in statistical or other advanced methodologies.

The doctoral program generally requires five years of full-time study. Students take courses during their first two years to prepare them for qualifying exams, which are generally taken at the end of the second year. Upon passing the qualifying exams, students advance to candidacy and begin work on their dissertations. Throughout their careers, students work closely with their advisors, who help them to prepare for their exams and develop their dissertation topics. All Ph.D. students are fully funded for five years. Funding packages include a tuition waiver, a generous stipend, and a health insurance subsidy.
ScholarshipAmount: Full tuition remission, coverage of university fees, and a stipend.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Global Communication and Applied Translation
Department: Dietrich College of Humanities and Social Sciences
Description: The M.A. in Global Communication and Applied Translation (GCAT) is a one-year, two-semester program for students who have advanced abilities in at least one language other than English (e.g., Chinese, French, German, Japanese, Spanish) and an interest in translation, localization, and global communication. The program focuses on translation technologies and project management for the localization industry. The program can be completed in two semesters of full-time study. GCAT is an excellent option for those who wish to pursue a career as a translator or localization project manager, as well as for those who wish to teach translation or pursue doctoral study in translation.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Second Language Acquisition
Department: Dietrich College of Humanities and Social Sciences
Description: The M.A. program in Second Language Acquisition (SLA) has a strong interdisciplinary focus. Its primary goal is to provide graduate students with a solid foundation in the key areas of linguistic theory, second language acquisition theory, and research methodology. Building on this foundation, students can focus on one or more areas of second language studies including the role of individual differences in second language learning, technology-enhanced language learning, classroom-based second language research, second language literacy, and second/foreign language pedagogy. The program is designed to prepare students for two main career tracks: 1. to enter a doctoral program in SLA or a related field; 2. to obtain a professional position as a foreign/second language specialist in a variety of national or international settings in the public or private sector.
ScholarshipType: Partial tuition scholarships, Teaching assistantships, Research assistantships

Department: Dietrich College of Humanities and Social Sciences
Description: The Ph.D. in Second Language Acquisition is an interdisciplinary program that focuses on the acquisition of second languages in both instructed and naturalistic settings. This empirically-driven program provides a strong foundation in theories of second language acquisition, research methodology, and the cognitive and neurological bases of bilingualism. Students in the program develop expertise in an area of specialization such as language program administration, technology-enhanced learning, classroom-based research, heritage language learning, sociolinguistics, or psycholinguistics. The program is committed to a mentorship model in which students work closely with faculty members on research projects. This research training prepares students for careers as faculty members in academic departments (e.g., Modern Languages, Second Language Studies, Applied Linguistics, English/ESL, Education) or as language specialists in government, the private sector, and non-profit organizations.

Department: Dietrich College of Humanities and Social Sciences
Description: The Ph.D. program in Philosophy is a research-oriented program designed to prepare students for careers in research and teaching. The Department of Philosophy at Carnegie Mellon is a world leader in a variety of research areas, including logic, philosophy of science, philosophy of language, philosophy of mind, formal epistemology, and ethics. The graduate program is a small and focused program in which students and faculty have the opportunity for regular and close interaction. All graduate students receive five years of funding, and they are offered ample opportunities for teaching and teaching preparation.

Department: Dietrich College of Humanities and Social Sciences
Concentration: ['Cognitive Psychology', 'Cognitive Neuroscience', 'Developmental Psychology', 'Educational Psychology', 'Social/Personality/Health Psychology']
Description: The Department of Psychology offers a program leading to the Ph.D. degree that is distinguished by its focus on psychological science. The department does not offer a clinical training program. The graduate program focuses on a number of areas including cognitive psychology, cognitive neuroscience, developmental psychology, educational psychology, and social/personality/health psychology. Students in each of these areas are encouraged to develop a program of courses and research that meets their own specific interests, taking advantage of the unique strengths available within the department and, more broadly, within the university. The program is designed to be completed in five years. All students are admitted for the fall semester.

ProgramName: Ph.D. in Social and Decision Sciences
Department: Dietrich College of Humanities and Social Sciences
Description: The Ph.D. program in social and decision sciences is a research-based program that trains students in the tradition of the "Carnegie School" to conduct research on problems of theory and application that cross traditional disciplinary boundaries. Students take core courses in the fields that form the foundations of decision sciences—cognitive psychology, social psychology, organizational behavior, economics, political science and statistics—and then specialize in one or more of these areas. In addition to our core faculty, students have access to the broad range of faculty talent available at Carnegie Mellon. The program is small, selective and informal, and is characterized by close work between students and faculty. The program prepares students primarily for academic careers in universities and research institutions.
ScholarshipType: Fellowship/Funding Package including tuition waiver, stipend, and health insurance

ProgramName: Ph.D. in Statistics and Data Science
Department: Dietrich College of Humanities and Social Sciences
Description: The Ph.D. program in the Department of Statistics & Data Science at Carnegie Mellon University is arguably the premier doctoral program in the world for statistics. We train students to become researchers and leaders in the field of statistics and data science, both in academia and in industry. The training is a mix of core statistical theory and methodology, and a wide variety of specialty topics. Our Ph.D. students take courses from and conduct research with our world-renowned faculty, developing expertise in areas such as theory and foundations of statistics and probability, statistical methodology, computational statistics, interdisciplinary research, and statistical practice.

Department: Heinz College of Information Systems and Public Policy
Concentration: ['Cultural Leadership, Policy and Advocacy', 'Live Entertainment Management', 'Visual Arts Management', 'Artistic and Curatorial Practice']
Description: The Master of Arts Management (M.A.M.) program prepares students to lead and manage arts and cultural organizations through a combination of rigorous coursework in management, data analysis, technology, and experiential learning. The two-year program is joint between the Heinz College of Information Systems and Public Policy and the College of Fine Arts. The curriculum is designed to give students a deep understanding of the arts and cultural landscape, as well as the practical skills needed to succeed in a variety of roles in the field. Students learn from faculty who are experts in their fields, and they have the opportunity to work with leading arts and cultural organizations in Pittsburgh and around the world. The M.A.M. program is committed to preparing students for leadership roles in the arts and cultural sector, and to fostering a more equitable and sustainable future for the arts.

Department: College of Fine Arts and Heinz College of Information Systems and Public Policy
Description: Carnegie Mellon University's Master of Entertainment Industry Management (MEIM) program is the best in the world at preparing students to be the next generation of leaders in the business of film, television, music, theater, and interactive media. Our graduates are more than just managers—they are creative executives with the analytical skills to solve problems and the finesse to excel in the complex, ever-changing entertainment landscape. In the MEIM program, you will gain a deep understanding of the entertainment industry, its structures, and its business practices. The program consists of a year of classes at Carnegie Mellon's Pittsburgh campus followed by a year of classes and a required, full-time internship in Los Angeles at CMU's Heinz College LA center.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Health Care Policy and Management
Concentration: Health Care Analytics, Health Care Management
Description: The Master of Science in Health Care Policy and Management (MSHCPM) is a two-year program that prepares students to become the next generation of health care leaders. At the intersection of policy, management and technology, MSHCPM graduates improve health care delivery through evidence-based management, data analytics and an understanding of the complex U.S. health care system. Students learn from faculty who are experts in operations management, economics, information systems, and public policy, all from a data-driven perspective. Required coursework includes health care systems, finance, analytics, economics, operations, information systems, and policy. Students also select from a wide variety of elective coursework that meets their career goals, and the program culminates in a final semester team-based project on a real-world problem for a real-world client.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Information Security
Description: The Master of Science in Information Security (MSIS) degree is offered by the Information Networking Institute in conjunction with the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering and the School of Computer Science. The MSIS program provides an ideal environment for students to become leaders in the field of information security and an in-depth understanding of the core principles of information security: systems security, network security, cryptography, and security policy. The curriculum is a combination of foundational and advanced courses, a capstone project and real-world experience through an internship. MSIS students work closely with our world-renowned faculty members to conduct leading-edge research in a wide range of areas such as trustworthy computing, cyber forensics, secure coding, and cloud and mobile security.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Information Systems
Concentration: ['Business Intelligence & Data Analytics (BIDA)', 'Digital Marketing & Commerce', 'IT Strategy & Management', 'Information Security', 'Managing AI & Robotics', 'Product Management']
Description: The Master of Information Systems Management (MISM) program blends technology and leadership for a 21st century career. You will develop sought-after skills that bridge the gap between technology and management, including data analytics, machine learning, and information security. Our industry-proven curriculum and practical experience focus on building your leadership skills and professional network, putting you on track for a high-impact, high-paying career. The MISM program is offered in three formats: the 16-month flagship MISM program, a 12-month program for students with more than three years of professional work experience, and a 21-month global MISM program in conjunction with our Adelaide, Australia campus. Each path includes the core coursework you will need to lead organizations in the new millennium.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Information Technology
Concentration: ['Information Security (MSIS)', 'Mobility (MSIT-MOB)', 'Software Management (MSIT-SM)', 'Artificial Intelligence & Innovation (MSIT-AII)']
Description: The Master of Science in Information Technology (MSIT) degree is conferred for programs in Information Security (MSIS), Mobility (MSIT-MOB), Software Management (MSIT-SM) and Artificial Intelligence & Innovation (MSIT-AII). Each program combines a rigorous technical curriculum, practical, industry-oriented topics and a required internship or practicum to prepare students to be the next generation of leaders in the ICT industry.

The Master of Medical Management (MMM) is a 12-month, 108-unit graduate business degree for mid-career physicians and executives working in health care organizations. The program is designed to develop the professional management and leadership skills of these individuals. To accomplish this, the MMM curriculum emphasizes core business knowledge and health systems management skills and tools. The program is taught in a synchronous blended format of online learning and in-person instruction at CMU's Pittsburgh campus. The curriculum is delivered over four 12-week semesters, with students taking three courses per semester. Students take courses in financial and managerial accounting, operations management, corporate finance, marketing, organizational design and behavior, information systems, decision analysis, negotiations, health economics, and leadership development.

Concentration: ['Digital Transformation and Analytics', 'Leading and Managing People and Organizations', 'Public Finance', 'Smart Communities', 'Social Innovation and Entrepreneurship', 'Strategy and Management Consulting', 'Defense and Security Policy (Washington, DC only)', 'Cybersecurity Policy (Washington, DC only)']
Description: The Master of Public Management (MPM) program prepares experienced professionals for career advancement as managers, executives, and leaders in government, non-profit organizations, and the private sector. The MPM program is designed to hone students’ general management knowledge and to sharpen their analytical and leadership skills. A flexible curriculum allows students to design a program of study that is specific to their personal interests and career goals. Students customize their degree plan by complementing the management and analytics core with a rich selection of elective courses.
Accredidation: The Master of Science in Public Policy and Management (MSPPM), the Master of Public Management (MPM), and the Master of Science in Health Care Policy and Management (MSHCPM) are accredited by the Network of Schools of Public Policy, Affairs, and Administration (NASPAA).

ProgramName: Master of Science in Public Policy and Management
Concentration: ['MSPPM: Washington D.C.', 'MSPPM: Data Analytics', 'MSPPM: Digital Transformation and Analytics', 'MSPPM: Fast Track', 'MSPPM: Global', 'MSPPM: Standard 2-year']
Description: The Master of Science in Public Policy and Management (MSPPM) program is for students who want to become public policy leaders in government, nonprofit organizations, or the private sector. The program blends a deep foundation in policy analysis, management, and technology with hands-on, real-world experience. The MSPPM program offers several pathways, which are specializations that enable students to gain significant depth in a specific area of study. All MSPPM students are required to complete an internship during the summer between their first and second years. Students also are required to complete a team-based project, called a Capstone Project (formerly Systems Synthesis), during their final two semesters. This project gives them an opportunity to perform in-depth analysis of a policy or management problem for a real-world client.
Accredidation: The Master of Science in Public Policy and Management (MSPPM), the Master of Science in Health Care Policy and Management (MSHCPM), and the Master of Public Management (MPM) are accredited by the Network of Schools of Public Policy, Affairs, and Administration (NASPAA).

ProgramName: Ph.D. in Public Policy and Management
Description: The Ph.D. in Public Policy and Management at the Heinz College combines a deep disciplinary grounding with a problem-focused, empirical, and interdisciplinary approach to education and research. This philosophy is reflected in the faculty, which is drawn from fields including economics, sociology, political science, organizational behavior, operations research, and information technology. It is also reflected in the Ph.d. program's core curriculum, which draws from all of these disciplines.

Concentration: ['Biochemistry and Biophysics', 'Cell and Developmental Biology', 'Computational Biology', 'Genetics and Molecular Biology', 'Neuroscience']
Description: The Ph.D. program in Biological Sciences is an interdisciplinary research-oriented program that provides students with the best possible foundation to become leaders in the field of biomedical research. We train our students to think creatively and quantitatively and to tackle challenging problems at the forefront of the biological sciences. The first year of study includes a core course, quantitative coursework and electives, and a series of three rotations in different laboratories. At the end of the first year, students select a thesis adviser and begin their dissertation research. Subsequent years of study are devoted primarily to laboratory research. All students are required to serve as a teaching assistant for two semesters. Ph.D. students receive full tuition support, a stipend and health insurance.

Concentration: ['Biological Chemistry', 'Materials Chemistry', 'Polymer Chemistry', 'Green Chemistry']
Description: The Ph.D. in Chemistry is a research-based degree program. The curriculum is designed to give students the best possible preparation for becoming independent scientists. Ph.D. students in chemistry take advanced graduate courses, pass a series of qualifying examinations and conduct a significant, multi-year research project that culminates in a dissertation. Research in the department is divided into four main areas: Biological Chemistry, Materials Chemistry, Polymer Chemistry, and Green Chemistry. However, many faculty and student research projects are interdisciplinary and cross these traditional boundaries. The Department of Chemistry encourages interdisciplinary research and collaboration between research groups.

The graduate program in mathematics is a doctoral program leading to the Ph.D. degree. Its goal is to train students to become research mathematicians. We seek to provide an environment in which students can develop to their fullest potential. This includes a broad and deep graduate curriculum, seminars on a wide range of topics of current research interest, and a great deal of informal interaction with faculty and fellow graduate students. Students have great freedom in choosing their courses and their research advisors. We place a high priority on the quality of our teaching and advising. We are proud of the fact that the Department's graduate students regularly win teaching awards.

Concentration: ['Biological Physics', 'Condensed Matter Physics', 'Cosmology and Astrophysics', 'Particle Physics']
Description: The Ph.D. program in the Department of Physics is a flexible program of study aimed at training the next generation of leaders in academic, industrial, and national laboratory physics research. The program is tailored to the individual student with the goals of bringing each to the forefront of a subfield of physics and of developing his or her abilities to think critically, to carry out independent research, and to communicate the results of that research effectively. There are strong research programs in biological physics, condensed matter physics, cosmology and astrophysics, and particle physics. These programs are enhanced by the presence of a number of multidisciplinary research centers, by strong interdepartmental programs, and by the close collaboration of faculty from different departments.

The Master of Science in Computer Science offers students with a bachelor's degree the opportunity to improve their training with advanced study in computer science. This is a degree that can be completed in three semesters, and that provides an enduring foundation for future professional growth. The M.S. program combines a solid and practical core with the flexibility to pursue individual interests. Students can choose a course-based option, or they can choose to complete an M.S. project, supervised by one of our world-class faculty. Graduates of this program will be well-prepared for a high-level research or development position in industry.

The Computer Science Department (CSD) offers a Ph.D. in Computer Science that is one of the premier programs in the world. Our world-class faculty conduct research in a variety of areas, including: Algorithms, Complexity and Theory; Artificial Intelligence; Computer Architecture; Graphics, Vision and Games; Human-Computer Interaction; Languages, Compilers and Systems; Machine Learning and Big Data; Robotics; Security and Privacy; Social, Cultural and Ethical Issues in Computer Science; and Systems and Networking. We are home to 500+ Ph.D. students who come from across the globe and who receive full financial support. We invite you to explore our website, learn about our research and our graduate programs, and apply for admission. The Ph.D. program in CSD is for students who have a bachelor’s or a master's degree. Students are admitted to the Ph.D. program in the fall semester only. In their first year, all Ph.D. students are supported by a fellowship. Students are expected to join a research project as a research assistant in their first semester and to have a research advisor by the end of their second semester. After their first year, students are generally supported as research assistants by their advisors. All Ph.D. students are also required to serve as a teaching assistant for two semesters. We believe the teaching experience is a vital part of graduate education, giving students the opportunity to deepen their own knowledge of a subject while developing their skills in both research and teaching.

The M.S. in Computational Biology program provides students with the knowledge and skills to be successful researchers in the exciting, interdisciplinary field of computational biology. This program is offered by the Department of Computational Biology within the School of Computer Science, and is geared toward students with a bachelor’s degree in computer science, biology, or a related field. Students take courses in both computer science and biology, as well as specialized courses in computational biology. The curriculum ensures that students will be able to design and implement significant computational systems. Students are also exposed to a broad range of research areas in computational biology, and will conduct in-depth research with a faculty member in a particular area of interest. Research opportunities are available in areas such as computational genomics, biological imaging, computational structural biology, and systems biology. Students are encouraged to meet with faculty to discuss their research interests. Students should be able to complete this program in three to four semesters.

The Ph.D. program in Computational Biology is a unique interdisciplinary program that was created with the belief that the future of biology depends on the successful integration of biological and computational sciences. To develop as a scientist who is a “biologist in a computational world,” a student must become knowledgeable in biology, computer science and machine learning. The Ph.D. program is structured to provide an integrated curriculum covering these areas. The primary mission of the Ph.D. program is to train the next generation of leaders in the field. The objectives are: to provide students with the knowledge of modern biology and the computational and quantitative skills to carry out research in computational biology, to develop students' ability to carry out high-quality independent research and to develop students' written and oral communication skills.

The Master of Human-Computer Interaction (MHCI) program is the first program in the world dedicated to preparing professionals for careers related to human-computer interaction, user experience design and user-centered research. Our curriculum provides a scientific and practical understanding of how to design, build and evaluate new user experiences and technologies. This professional master's program is a three-semester, 12-month program beginning in late summer (August) and ending the following August. The program provides a breadth of HCI methods and techniques and provides opportunities to practice those skills in a range of project courses. The capstone project is the culmination of the program, and is an 8-month team-based project working with an external industry client. MHCI students are very successful in finding excellent jobs after graduation in a wide range of organizations, and often become leaders in the field.

The Ph.D. in Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) is for students who want to conduct scientific research in HCI. The program trains students in the research methods and scholarship of a number of different disciplines, such that graduates will be competent to conduct research in HCI from a number of different perspectives. At the same time, each student pursues in-depth research with one or two advisors, such that they become a world-class expert in a particular subarea of HCI. Typical research areas for HCI Ph.D. students include social computing, learning sciences, design, and human-robot interaction, but students can pursue research in any area of HCI where there are faculty with whom to work. Students are fully funded (tuition, fees, and a stipend) as research assistants on faculty-led research projects.

ProgramName: M.S. in Artificial Intelligence and Innovation
Description:
The Master of Science in Artificial Intelligence and Innovation (MSAII) program is a professional master’s degree program offered through the Language Technologies Institute (LTI). The MSAII program grounds students in the principles of AI, while providing hands-on experience in the application of these principles in real-world settings. MSAII students complete a summer internship and an industry-sponsored capstone project.

The MSAII degree program takes 16 months of study to complete. Students will start in the fall semester and graduate in the second spring semester. During their summer, students are expected to complete a paid internship that is related to the MSAII program.

The curriculum begins with a set of core courses that are designed to ground all students in the foundations of the relevant areas of artificial intelligence. In addition, students have the opportunity to take a number of electives from across the university to gain more depth in specific areas of interest.

The highlight of the curriculum is the MSAII Capstone project, a team-based, two-semester course where students will work closely with an industry sponsor to solve a real-world problem. The Capstone will challenge students to draw on the knowledge and skills they have gained through the MSAII program to deliver a significant system for their sponsor.

The MSAII degree will prepare students to take on technical leadership roles in the development and deployment of AI-enabled systems in a variety of industries.

The Master of Computational Data Science (MCDS) is an elite, 16-month professional master’s program that teaches students how to use cutting-edge, large-scale machine learning and data science techniques in a distributed computing environment. A key element of the MCDS program is the capstone project course, in which students spend a whole semester tackling a real-world data science problem for a real-world client. Students learn how to apply their skills in a practical setting, how to manage a long-term project and how to communicate effectively with clients.

Concentration: Applied Machine Learning, Computational Finance, Geoinformatics, Language Technologies, Personalized and Social Systems, Text Analysis
Description: The Master of Science in Intelligent Information Systems (MIIS) degree provides students with an in-depth knowledge of the computational technology needed for managing and making sense of the vast amounts of information now available online. The MIIS program trains students in a core of relevant technologies including information retrieval, machine learning, data mining, and language technologies. It also allows students to choose in-depth coursework in specialty areas where intelligent information systems are critical, such as computational finance or geography. MIIS students are able to create their own individualized program by combining core courses, concentration courses, and free electives. The program includes the option of a one-semester practicum. The MIIS program is for students who want a professional Master’s degree that will prepare them for industry.

ProgramName: M.S. in Intelligent Information Systems - Advanced Study
Description:
The Master of Science in Intelligent Information Systems (MIIS) is a two-year professional master’s degree program for students with an undergraduate degree in Computer Science or a related discipline. The program is offered by the Language Technologies Institute (LTI). It is designed to train students in collecting, processing,analyzing and retrieving information from structured and unstructured data, with courses from areas such as language technologies, machine learning, information retrieval, cloud computing, and big data techniques.

The Advanced Study option of the MIIS program requires students to work on a large independent project. In addition to gaining a deep expertise in Intelligent Information Systems, the students in the Advanced Study option learn to plan and manage a large research or development project, to solve complex open-ended problems, and to effectively communicate the results in written and oral forms. This option is aimed at students who want to develop strong research or development skills.

The Master of Science in Language Technologies (MS in LT) is an ideal choice for students who want to improve their skills in one or more of the many areas of language technology. The program is specifically designed to prepare its graduates for a successful career in the language technologies industry, but it can also serve as an excellent springboard to PhD programs for those who are interested in pursuing research. The MS in LT program takes 3 semesters (Fall, Spring, Fall) to complete. During this time, students will take a combination of core, restricted-elective, and unrestricted-elective courses, and complete an MS project.

ProgramName: Ph.D. in Language and Information Technologies
Description: The Ph.D. program in Language and Information Technologies is for students who want to perform research in the core areas of language and information technologies, with the goal of becoming a university professor or an industrial researcher. The program grounds students in the core knowledge of the field through a sequence of foundational coursework in computational linguistics, information retrieval, machine learning, and computer science. Students then select one or two research areas to focus on and go on to perform original research, culminating in a Ph.D. dissertation that makes a substantial, original contribution to the field. This may be followed by a postdoctoral research fellowship and/or an academic or industrial research position.

The M.S. in Machine Learning program gives students a deep knowledge of the concepts and methods of machine learning, and provides them with the ability to apply this knowledge to solve real-world problems. The program immerses students in the multicultural, collaborative, and interdisciplinary environment that makes Carnegie Mellon a world leader in machine learning education. Students complete their degrees in three semesters: Fall, Spring, and a final Fall. The M.S. program combines classroom instruction with practical experience. The first two semesters consist mainly of coursework, while the final semester focuses on a capstone project. In the capstone project, students work in teams to solve a real-world problem. This team-based approach, along with the project's demanding expectations, helps students refine their project management and communication skills. Our students also participate in our weekly Machine Learning Lunch talk series, and many of them work with our world-renowned faculty on research projects. Graduates of the program are well-prepared for jobs in industry, or for Ph.D. programs.

The Ph.D. program in Machine Learning is for students who are interested in research in Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence. This program is a collaboration between four sponsoring departments: the Machine Learning Department, the Computer Science Department, the Department of Statistics & Data Science, and the Department of Philosophy (Dietrich College of Humanities & Social Sciences). Students have the opportunity to do research in a wide variety of areas, including machine learning, artificial intelligence, statistics, computer science, philosophy, computational and statistical neuroscience, robotics, natural language processing, and computer vision. The degree is granted through the Machine Learning Department.

The Master of Science in Robotics (MSR) program trains students to be tomorrow’s leaders in the ever-growing field of robotics. This unique, research-based master's degree program gives students the tools, experience and guidance they need to succeed.

The MSR program immerses students in a hands-on, project-based curriculum, helping them develop the skills to create and implement innovative robotics systems and solutions. Our students work side by side with top researchers to tackle real-world problems. This flexible degree allows students to create their own specialized curriculum, drawing from courses across the university in areas like machine learning, computer vision, control, mechatronics and artificial intelligence.

The curriculum consists of a breadth component, a depth component, and an MS thesis or MS project. The breadth component is made of core courses covering the fundamentals of robotics, and the depth component allows students to gain deep expertise in their chosen area. Finally, the MS thesis/project is the culminating experience in which students are challenged to apply the material learned in their coursework toward independent research in the field of robotics under the supervision of a faculty advisor. The result of this two-year program is a new generation of roboticists ready to tackle the world’s next great challenges. We aim to produce graduates who will go on to be the next leaders in the field.

The Ph.D. in Robotics is a research-based degree program that prepares students for research careers in academia, industry or government. Students develop the ability to create new knowledge in robotics and to function as an independent researcher. In addition, the Robotics Institute offers an affiliated Ph.D. program in Machine Learning.

ProgramName: M. of Software Engineering in Embedded Systems
Description: The MS-SE-ES program is a 16-month, 3-semester program offered jointly by the Institute for Software Research (ISR), the Electrical and Computer Engineering Department (ECE), and the Robotics Institute (RI). This program trains students in the foundations of software engineering with a focus on the unique challenges of embedded systems. Graduates will be uniquely qualified for positions in a variety of industries including automotive, avionics, consumer electronics, and medical devices.

ProgramName: M. of Software Engineering in Scalable Systems
Description: The Master of Science in Software Engineering - Scalable Systems (MS-SE-SS) program prepares software engineers to work on large-scale software systems that are used by millions of people, that process terabytes of data, and that exist on the cloud. Such systems are central to the success of many businesses, including Google, Amazon, Facebook, and Microsoft, and are increasingly important in scientific research, including supercomputing and “big data” analytics. The MS-SE-SS program teaches the principles of building such systems from the underlying computer systems principles to the business and management principles that are key to success.

Concentration: Software Architecture, Software Project Management
Description: The Master of Software Engineering (MSE) professional master's degree program provides students with a solid foundation in software engineering principles and practices, and an opportunity to specialize in a specific area of interest. It is designed for students with a bachelor's degree in a computing-related discipline and a few years of software development experience who wish to pursue a career as a software engineering professional. The program offers an unparalleled, career-focused curriculum, which combines a strong foundation in software engineering fundamentals with opportunities for hands-on, practical experience in our unique, studio-based courses.

The Master of Software Engineering (MSE) professional master's program is for students who want to build a professional career as a software engineer. The core of the program focuses on the principles and practices of software engineering, including requirements, design, construction and quality and management. Students complete a common core of courses that provide a strong foundation of knowledge in software engineering. These courses address topics including managing software development, software requirements and design, software architecture, and analysis of software artifacts. The MSE program includes a major, required, team-based studio project in which students develop a substantial software system for a real-world client. Students learn and practice their skills in a realistic development environment. The studio project is one of the features that distinguish this program.

The Master of Science in Privacy Engineering (MSPE) is a one-year graduate program for computer scientists and engineers who wish to pursue careers as privacy engineers. Students gain a foundation in privacy principles and learn to apply skills in system design and the development of privacy-enhancing technologies. The program is offered jointly by the School of Computer Science and the College of Engineering. Students will take courses in two different departments: the Information Networking Institute in the College of Engineering and a computer science department in the School of Computer Science. The MSPE program is intended for students with a bachelor’s degree in computer science or a related field. Students are expected to have a strong background in computer science, including coursework in data structures, algorithms, programming skills in Java, C, or C++, and systems programming. Some familiarity with computer security is helpful but not required. Graduates of the program will be able to define privacy policies, design and implement systems that comply with these policies, and conduct privacy risk analysis for data-centric systems.

ProgramName: M.S. in Privacy Engineering - Applied Study
Description: The Master of Science in Privacy Engineering (MSPE) is a one-year program for computer scientists and engineers who wish to pursue careers as privacy engineers or technical privacy managers. Privacy is a growing concern for companies of all sizes, government agencies and individuals. As our lives become increasingly digital, there is a growing need for technical solutions to protect our privacy. Privacy engineers are in great demand. The MSPE program is offered by the School of Computer Science (SCS) and the College of Engineering (CoE) at Carnegie Mellon University. This program, one of the first of its kind, trains students to build privacy-preserving systems, and to ensure that data collection, sharing and usage practices are compliant with privacy policies and regulations. The curriculum is a mix of technology and policy courses taught by faculty from the School of Computer Science, the College of Engineering, and the Heinz College. Students learn about privacy principles, and how to design and build systems that comply with these principles. The MSPE is a three-semester program. Students begin the program in the fall semester and graduate the following fall. Students will complete a capstone project during their final semester. Students enrolled through SCS will also complete a required summer internship.

ProgramName: M.S. in Privacy Technology and Policy
Description: The Master of Science in Privacy Technology and Policy (MSPTP) is a one-year graduate program that trains students to address the significant challenges of maintaining privacy in a world of ubiquitous data collection, aggregation, and dissemination. Privacy is a complex issue, requiring a holistic understanding from technological, legal, and policy perspectives. To address the demand for privacy professionals, Carnegie Mellon University has developed the MSPTP program to produce a new generation of leaders in the field. MSPTP graduates bring a unique combination of technology and policy expertise to their work, and have a deep understanding of the risks, challenges, and opportunities in the area of data privacy. The MSPTP program is a collaboration between the School of Computer Science (SCS) and the Heinz College of Information Systems and Public Policy.

The M.S. in Societal Computing answers a growing demand from industry and government for professionals with the ability to understand and build systems that work in a social context. The degree program offers a unique combination of computer science, social science and policy, preparing graduates to lead this new field of computing. Societal Computing focuses on the design, development, deployment and regulation of computing technologies that address important societal needs. Societal Computing applications often involve many people and devices, and may focus on a variety of societal domains, such as healthcare, urban transportation, disaster response, education, and sustainability. The curriculum includes courses in programming, machine learning, security, privacy, and research methods. A unique capstone project is a key feature of the program.

The Ph.D. program in Societal Computing is for students who want to develop new theories and technologies that address major societal challenges. Societal Computing is a new field of research that addresses such challenges by producing and evaluating new socio-technical systems. Our Ph.D. students typically have an undergraduate degree in computer science or a related discipline, though we also accept outstanding students with undergraduate degrees in the social sciences or humanities who have strong technical skills. Our program provides rigorous training in the research methodologies that are most relevant to societal computing research. These methods include machine learning, natural language processing, network analysis, experimental design, survey methods, and qualitative methods. In addition to gaining broad exposure to these methods, students work closely with our faculty to design, build and evaluate new technologies to address societal problems. Many of our students have engaged in research that has lead to the creation of deployed systems used by thousands of people or that has had a direct impact on public policy. Many of our students do interdisciplinary research and are co-advised by a faculty member in another department at Carnegie Mellon. Our students are well prepared for careers in academia, industrial research labs, government research labs and non-profits.

The Ph.D. in Software Engineering program is a research-based doctoral program for students who are interested in pursuing a career in research, whether in academia or in industry. The program provides a disciplined approach to the study of the software engineering process. Students in this program are well prepared for performing research on a wide range of topics that are relevant to the software engineering discipline. The program consists of coursework, including a common set of core courses, as well as a significant research project leading to a Ph.D. dissertation.

Concentration: ['Accounting', 'Business Technologies', 'Communications', 'Economics', 'Entrepreneurship', 'Finance', 'Healthcare Analytics', 'Marketing', 'Operations Management', 'Operations Research', 'Organizational Behavior', 'Strategy', 'Sustainability']
Description: The Master of Business Administration (M.B.A.) degree is offered as a full-time program. The curriculum consists of a combination of required and elective courses, a summer internship, and several professional development workshops and activities. Students are also required to choose an academic concentration and complete a minimum of three courses within the concentration. The concentrations represent a range of established and emerging business fields in which the faculty has particular expertise. Students are able to select a variety of elective courses in other Carnegie Mellon schools and colleges to fulfill their concentration requirement, creating a truly unique and specialized program of study.
Accredidation: AACSB

Concentration: ['Accounting', 'Business Technologies', 'Economics', 'Financial Economics', 'Marketing', 'Operations Management', 'Operations Research', 'Organizational Behavior and Theory']
Description: The Tepper School of Business doctoral program is a full-time course of study and apprenticeship that prepares students for scholarly careers in research and teaching. The curriculum is demanding and challenging, and is designed to develop in each student the capacity for doing high-quality, creative research. The program seeks to attract a small, select group of students from diverse backgrounds and to provide an environment that enables these students to fulfill their scholarly potential. The program offers eight major fields of study: accounting, business technology, economics, financial economics, marketing, operations management, operations research, and organizational behavior and theory. Students from all fields receive rigorous classroom training in a primary discipline and in the basic tools of research such as mathematics, economics, and statistics. Doctoral students are introduced early into the research activity in their major fields of study, where they work closely with faculty members on topics of mutual interest. The school provides an unusual degree of flexibility, which allows students to develop an individualized plan of study tailored to their own interests.
Accredidation: The Tepper School of Business is accredited by AACSB International–the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering
Concentration: ['Advanced Chemical Engineering', 'Bioengineered Drug Delivery & Development', 'Computational & Data-Driven Chemical Engineering', 'Energy & Climate', 'Entrepreneurship', 'Materials Science & Engineering', 'Process Systems Engineering', 'Research']
Description: The undergraduate program in chemical engineering provides a curriculum where the scientific and engineering content is thoroughly integrated and carefully sequenced to provide a cohesive and comprehensive education. From the very beginning, students are introduced to chemical engineering principles and practice through a series of courses that spiral throughout the curriculum, culminating in a year-long, capstone design course. A unique aspect of the undergraduate curriculum is its emphasis on process systems engineering, an area pioneered at Carnegie Mellon that provides students with the tools to manage the complexity that is inherent in the chemical and manufacturing industries.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering
Concentration: Advanced Infrastructure Systems, Environmental Engineering, and Mechanics, Materials and Computing
Description: Civil engineers design and build the world’s infrastructure, and address critical societal challenges, such as climate change adaptation and mitigation. The undergraduate curriculum provides a foundation in engineering sciences and design that you’ll apply to solve challenges in the natural and built environment. You can personalize your degree through technical concentrations in areas like Advanced Infrastructure Systems, Environmental Engineering, and Mechanics, Materials and Computing, or through a variety of minors and second majors. Our department has a vibrant student community where you’ll engage in hands-on learning through project courses, student clubs and undergraduate research.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Electrical and Computer Engineering
Concentration: Device Science & Nanofabrication, Circuits & Systems, Signals & Systems, Computer Hardware & Systems, Software & Systems
Description: The undergraduate programs in electrical and computer engineering at Carnegie Mellon provide a balance of fundamental theory and practical application to prepare our students for the real-world problems they will face throughout their careers. A flexible curriculum, with a rich set of electives and a number of double major and minor options, enables our students to customize their academic experience and to pursue their interests. In addition, the college-wide emphasis on interdisciplinary study and research makes ECE an exciting place to learn and grow.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Electrical and Computer Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Engineering
Description: Environmental Engineering focuses on the scientific and engineering principles needed to protect and clean the environment and to provide for a sustainable future. In the Bachelor of Science in Environmental Engineering (EnvE) program, you’ll focus on fundamental areas of the discipline, including water and air quality, hydrology, environmental chemistry, and environmental modeling. You’ll become equipped with the tools needed to design and create a sustainable world by developing green products and creating sustainable energy solutions. You’ll be prepared to recognize and address the environmental consequences of human activities and to design systems to minimize their negative impacts.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Environmental Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Materials Science and Engineering
Requirements: First-year applicants to Carnegie Mellon are required to submit the Common Application, a $75 application fee or waiver, an official high school transcript, a Secondary School Counselor Evaluation, one Teacher Recommendation, and answers to the Carnegie Mellon Writing Questions. Submission of SAT or ACT scores is optional. English Proficiency Testing is required for students whose native language is not English.
Concentration: Biomaterials, Electronic materials, Materials for energy, Mechanical behavior, Metallurgy, Nanomaterials, Polymers, Sustainability
Description: Materials are everywhere. Everything is made of something, and that something is a material. From transportation to electronics, advanced medical devices to sustainable energy, materials science and engineering (MSE) is at the forefront of technology and the student who graduates with a materials science degree from Carnegie Mellon University will have a bright future. Our students learn the fundamentals of materials science and engineering through a core curriculum and then can specialize in a specific area by choosing from a variety of electives. Our undergraduate students get hands-on experience by completing lab courses as part of their curriculum. Research opportunities with our world-renowned faculty allow students to gain valuable research experience. In addition, many of our students take advantage of study abroad opportunities, co-ops and internships to broaden their education.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Materials Science and Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering
Requirements: All first-year applicants must submit the following for a complete application: Common Application, a non-refundable $75 application fee or an approved fee waiver, official high school transcript, one teacher recommendation, a Secondary School Counselor Recommendation, and the Common Application Essay and Writing Supplement. For students applying for Fall 2025 admission, standardized test scores (SAT/ACT) are optional. For students who've taken college courses while in high school, an official college/university transcript is required. English Language Proficiency Testing is required for applicants whose native language is not English.
Concentration: Aerospace Engineering, Biomechanics, Computational Engineering, Energy & the Environment, Manufacturing & Materials, Product Design, Robotics
Description: Mechanical engineering is a broad and diverse discipline of engineering that applies the principles of physics and materials science for the analysis, design, manufacturing, and maintenance of mechanical systems. At Carnegie Mellon University, our Mechanical Engineering program prepares you to become a leader in this ever-changing field. Our curriculum provides you with a strong foundation in the fundamentals of mechanical engineering, including mechanics, thermodynamics, fluid dynamics, and heat transfer. You will also have the opportunity to specialize in a number of areas, including robotics, biomechanics, and energy systems. Our faculty are world-renowned experts in their fields, and they are committed to providing you with a high-quality education. You will have the opportunity to learn from the best and to work on cutting-edge research projects. We also have a number of state-of-the-art facilities, including a wind tunnel, a water tunnel, and a robotics lab. You will have the opportunity to use these facilities to conduct experiments and to develop your skills.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET.

Concentration: Bioimaging and Biophotonics, Biomechanics and Biomaterials, Cellular and Molecular Bioengineering, Computational Biomedical Engineering
Description: The undergraduate curriculum in biomedical engineering is offered as an additional major to students who have a declared primary major in one of the traditional engineering disciplines offered at Carnegie Mellon. The flexible curriculum provides a strong background in the fundamentals of biomedical engineering as well as in-depth knowledge in specific areas of interest through a variety of elective courses.

ProgramName: Additional Major in Engineering and Public Policy
Description: Technological change lies at the heart of many pressing contemporary public policy issues, including those related to the environment, energy, information and communication, national security, and transportation. The additional major in Engineering and Public Policy (EPP) is designed to give engineering and computer science students a special set of skills that will allow them to better understand and deal with these complex problems. The curriculum provides a foundation for students in two broad areas: social analysis, with an emphasis on the fundamental concepts of economics, statistics, and decision science; and technology and policy analysis, a set of skills for applying social and technical analysis to policy issues in which technology is a critical factor.

ProgramName: Additional Major in Engineering Design, Innovation & Entrepreneurship
Requirements: The additional major is open to any student in the College of Engineering. You may declare the additional major as early as the spring of your first year, and no later than the fall of your junior year. You must use the Intent to Declare form to begin the process.
Concentration: Design, Entrepreneurship
Description: The Additional Major in Engineering Design, Innovation, and Entrepreneurship (EDIE) is a program offered through the Integrated Innovation Institute that focuses on creating value through new products, services, and ventures. It provides engineering students with a foundation in the principles and practices of innovation and entrepreneurship, combining design-centric thinking with technology and business. The additional major allows students to choose a concentration in either Design or Entrepreneurship, which will be specified on their transcript. The curriculum for the program is anchored by a two-semester capstone course in which student teams create a new product or service venture. It is the undergraduate component of the College of Engineering's three-tiered, cross-campus entrepreneurship educational ladder.

Requirements:
All first-year applicants must submit the following:
- Common Application
- Official High School Transcript
- One Teacher Recommendation
- Guidance Counselor Recommendation
- Common Application Essay and Carnegie Mellon Writing Questions
- Standardized Test Scores (Optional for 2025 Applicants)
- English Proficiency Test Scores (if applicable)
- Application Fee or Waiver
- Portfolio of creative work is required for all applicants to the School of Architecture.
Concentration: ['Sustainable Design', 'Computational Design', 'Building Performance', 'Urban Design']
Description: The five-year Bachelor of Architecture (B.Arch) is a first-professional undergraduate degree that is nationally accredited by the National Architectural Accrediting Board (NAAB). The B.Arch curriculum is centered on the design studio, a project-based learning environment in which students develop their design skills and abilities. In addition to a rigorous design curriculum, B.Arch students take required courses in building technology, computational design, architectural history and theory, and representation. These are supported by a combination of School of Architecture (SoA), College of Fine Arts (CFA), and university-wide electives that allow students to pursue their unique interests. The B.Arch program enables students to concentrate in an area of their interest through the selection of advanced synthesis option studios (ASOS) and SoA electives in their fourth and fifth years. These studios and electives are clustered in four areas of focus: Sustainable Design; Computational Design; Building Performance; and Urban Design. The School of Architecture encourages students to develop their own focus and deepen their expertise in a particular area of interest through a variety of advanced courses including ASOS, SoA seminars and workshops, and university-wide electives. Many students take advantage of the university’s strengths in other disciplines by pursuing minors and second majors.
Accredidation: Carnegie Mellon University, School of Architecture offers the following NAAB-accredited degree program: Bachelor of Architecture (B.Arch), 160 credits.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Architecture (B.A. in Architecture)
Description: The B.A. in Architecture is a four-year liberal arts degree in architecture. Students in this program benefit from the extensive offerings of a research university by taking more than half their classes in the fine arts, humanities, social sciences and natural sciences. The curriculum provides a platform for a variety of career paths inside and outside of design and the built environment. After graduation, B.A. in Architecture students can work in a variety of fields or apply to a two-year Master of Architecture (M.Arch) program to pursue professional licensure. The B.A. curriculum doesn't include the professional studio sequence required for licensure.
Accredidation: The B.A. is not a professionally accredited degree.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Art
Requirements: All first-year applicants must submit the Common Application & Carnegie Mellon Writing Supplement, application fee, official high school transcript, one teacher recommendation, and a school counselor recommendation. For applicants to the School of Art, a portfolio is also required.
Department: School of Art, College of Fine Arts
Concentration: ['Drawing, Painting, Print Media, & Photography', 'Electronic & Time-Based Media', 'Sculpture, Installation & Site-Work']
Description: The BFA program is an artist’s-level professional degree that provides a broad and deep foundation in contemporary art. Students select from a wide range of courses in order to explore and develop a specific focus for their artistic practice. With extensive required coursework in both art history and academic subjects, the BFA provides students with a rich and comprehensive education. The first year of the BFA program is a shared experience of courses in drawing, sculpture, time-based media, and media specific studios. In subsequent years, students can concentrate in specific areas or work across media. With small classes, ample facilities, and an acclaimed faculty, the BFA program provides students with unparalleled opportunities for artistic and intellectual growth.

Concentration: ['Products (industrial design)', 'Communications (graphic design)', 'Environments (physical and digital)']
Description: Our undergraduate program in design is a four-year, pre-professional degree that educates students to be nimble, thoughtful and skilled practitioners of design. We define design broadly and prepare students to work in one or more of three tracks: Products (industrial design), Communications (graphic design) and Environments (physical and digital). This interdisciplinary education prepares students to be leaders in a variety of existing and emerging fields and to be adaptable to a professional world in constant flux.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Drama
Requirements: All first-year applicants must submit the Common Application, which includes the Carnegie Mellon Writing Questions, an official high school transcript, a teacher recommendation, a secondary school counselor evaluation, and the application fee. In addition, all applicants to the School of Drama must submit a pre-screen application for their chosen area of study (e.g., Acting, Design, Dramaturgy) via the Acceptd platform. Pre-screen requirements are specific to each option and may include a resume, headshot, essays, a portfolio, monologues, or songs. Based on this pre-screen, select applicants will be invited to an audition or interview.
Concentration: ['Acting / Music Theater', 'Design', 'Directing', 'Dramaturgy', 'Production Technology & Management']
Description: The undergraduate curriculum in the School of Drama provides a rich and comprehensive program of study for young theater artists. By combining a conservatory training program with a broad-based university education, students are prepared to be leaders in all areas of the theater. The BFA programs offered within the School of Drama are four-year, conservatory-style programs that combine rigorous, professional training with a traditional university education.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Music Composition
Description: The undergraduate composition program immerses you in the craft of making music. You’ll be exposed to a broad range of contemporary music, working with both traditional and electronic media. The program is flexible, allowing you to develop and follow your own interests, while offering rigorous training in the fundamentals of composition. In addition to a weekly private lesson, you will also take a weekly studio class with the entire composition studio. This allows for frequent opportunities to share and discuss your own work and learn from your peers. Each semester, you’ll have a new composition of yours performed on a student composition recital. In your fourth year, you’ll present a full recital of your own music. Throughout your four years, you’ll have the opportunity to have your work read and/or performed by the CMU Contemporary Ensemble and the CMU Philharmonic.
Accredidation: The School of Music is a member of the National Association of Schools of Music.
AverageScholarshipAmount: $51,400 (for first-year students awarded need-based aid in 2022-2023)
ScholarshipAmount: Presidential Scholarships range from $4,000 to $10,000 per year
ScholarshipPercentage: 44% of undergraduate students received grant or scholarship aid (2022-2023)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Electronic Music
Requirements: All applicants to the School of Music must submit the Common Application, including the Carnegie Mellon Writing Supplement, and the School of Music Application Supplement. Required application components include an official high school transcript, a teacher recommendation, an essay, and a resume. Applicants to the B.F.A. in Electronic Music must also submit a composition portfolio.
Department: School of Music, College of Fine Arts
Description: The undergraduate composition curriculum provides comprehensive professional training for students whose goal is to become a composer. It encompasses a broad range of stylistic possibilities, from traditional to experimental. Students are free to explore their individual voices in depth, working in acoustic and electronic media, for the concert hall, and for interdisciplinary projects. Through private lessons, group seminars, and a regular schedule of student composition concerts, undergraduates develop a strong command of compositional techniques and the ability to compose for a diverse array of musical forces.
Accredidation: Carnegie Mellon University is a member of and accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Instrumental Performance
Requirements: All applicants to the School of Music must complete the Common Application, the Carnegie Mellon Common Application Supplement, and a School of Music Application. The School of Music application will include a music resume/repertoire list. In addition to these forms, applicants must submit pre-screening recordings (if required for their instrument), a music teacher recommendation, and high school transcripts. After a successful pre-screening, applicants will be invited to perform an audition.
Description:
Students in Instrumental Performance learn from a faculty of active, professional musicians, many of whom are members of the world-renowned Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra.

The curriculum provides a broad range of solo, chamber, and large ensemble performance experiences combined with a comprehensive foundation in music theory and history. One-on-one studio instruction with our acclaimed faculty is central to the program.

In addition to a rigorous musical education, students pursue a wide range of academic interests through our university-wide general education program. Many music students choose to expand their studies through a music minor (such as music technology or music theory), a university minor, or even a second major in one of Carnegie Mellon’s other acclaimed colleges.
Accredidation: The Carnegie Mellon School of Music is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Piano Performance
Description: The Keyboard area at the Carnegie Mellon School of Music provides an optimal environment for the comprehensive development of pianists in the 21st century. Performance studies for undergraduate and graduate piano majors include an intensive exploration of solo repertoire, chamber music, and piano concerti from all periods. We encourage the study and performance of contemporary works, including those of our own student and faculty composers. The program features courses in piano literature, piano pedagogy, and collaborative skills, all taught by our internationally recognized faculty. The curriculum is flexible and designed to fit the needs of each student as a developing artist. Students benefit from the warm, supportive environment within the keyboard area, as well as from numerous opportunities to perform as soloists, in chamber ensembles, and with the Carnegie Mellon orchestras. The Dalcroze Eurhythmics program, renowned throughout the world, further distinguishes Carnegie Mellon’s School of Music by providing an invaluable resource to pianists for developing their inner hearing and rhythmic skills.
Accredidation: The Carnegie Mellon University School of Music is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Vocal Performance
Department: School of Music, College of Fine Arts
Description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts in Vocal Performance degree educates undergraduate students to the highest standards of vocal and musical artistry, to be creative and engaged musicians in our diverse and changing world. Our curriculum offers comprehensive, conservatory-style training in vocal technique, musicianship, and performance, while allowing students to take advantage of the vast resources and opportunities in Carnegie Mellon’s interdisciplinary environment. Our graduates are equipped with the skills and experience necessary for a successful career in a variety of fields, including opera, musical theater, concert, and vocal pedagogy.
Accredidation: The School of Music is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Music and Technology
Requirements: All first-year applicants must submit the Common Application, official high school transcript, a teacher recommendation, and a school counselor recommendation. For the Bachelor of Science in Music and Technology program, applicants are required to submit a portfolio via the School of Music's Acceptd portal. The portfolio must include a profile video, a performance video, three work samples, a resume describing your background and experience in both music and technology, and an essay describing your interest in the Music & Technology program at Carnegie Mellon.
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Music and Technology is a joint degree offered by the School of Music and the Department of Computer Science. This degree provides an ideal course of study for students who are passionate about music and technology and who want to pursue a career in an area that requires a deep understanding of both. The curriculum includes courses in music theory, music composition, music performance, computer programming, computer systems, and signal processing. In addition, students take a series of core courses that integrate both disciplines and work with faculty who are leaders in the field of music technology.

Requirements:
All applicants to Carnegie Mellon are required to submit the following:
- The Common Application
- CMU-Specific Essay Questions
- High School Transcript
- Teacher Recommendation (one)
- School Counselor Recommendation
- Standardized Test Scores (Test-Optional for 2024 entry)
- Application Fee or Waiver
Department: Dietrich College of Humanities and Social Sciences
Description: The B.A. in Applied Multilingual Studies is a professional- and application-oriented major for students with an interest in understanding and working with language in a variety of real-world contexts and professions. Drawing on the strengths of the department in second language acquisition, literary and cultural studies, and professional/technical communication, the curriculum trains students to apply their linguistic and cultural knowledge to professional contexts such as translation, localization, media, and language education. The major prepares students to analyze how language is used in a variety of cultural contexts and social settings, to solve language-related problems in professional and community settings, to think critically about language and culture, and to manage multilingual information. Students in this major choose to concentrate in either one or two languages of study, and gain professional experience through a required internship or other professionalization experience.
ScholarshipPercentage: 46% of undergraduate students received grant/scholarship aid from CMU

Department: Dietrich College of Humanities and Social Sciences
Description: The major in Chinese Studies is an interdisciplinary program that allows students to focus on the study of Chinese language and culture. The program provides a solid background for a variety of careers, including international business, law and finance, diplomacy, journalism, translation and interpretation, as well as for graduate study in related fields. The major includes courses taken in the Department of Modern Languages as well as in other departments such as History and English. All majors are required to study abroad in a Chinese-speaking country for at least one semester. Many students take advantage of the various summer study abroad programs offered as well.

Requirements: All applicants to Carnegie Mellon apply to a college or school, not a specific major. Applicants to the Dietrich College of Humanities and Social Sciences, where the B.A. in Creative Writing is housed, must submit the Common Application, Carnegie Mellon Writing Questions, an official high school transcript, one teacher recommendation, and one school counselor recommendation. Required high school coursework includes four years of English, four years of math, one year of a lab science (biology, chemistry or physics), one year of history/social science, and two years of a foreign language.
Department: Dietrich College of Humanities and Social Sciences
Description: The Creative Writing major at Carnegie Mellon offers a culturally and historically diverse curriculum in which students can develop their skills in fiction, poetry and non-fiction. Students will gain experience writing in at least two genres, with the opportunity to go deeper into their genre of choice and to develop an ambitious creative project in the form of a senior thesis. In small workshops and individual tutorials, students work closely with our world-renowned faculty of practicing writers who are committed to mentoring students one on one. Creative Writing majors also get a strong grounding in literary history and cultural analysis in our literature courses, and have opportunities to explore publishing, editing and public writing projects through our many related programs and our student-run literary magazine, The Oakland Review. The skills our majors learn—in critical reading, creative and analytical thinking, and effective communication—will prepare them for successful careers in an array of different fields.
ScholarshipPercentage: 49.1% of first-year students were awarded need-based scholarships

ProgramName: B.A. in Film and Visual Media
Department: Dietrich College of Humanities and Social Sciences
Description: The major in Film and Visual Media provides students with a foundational knowledge of cinematic language and history while guiding them as they find their own creative voice. Our program integrates film studies and production, encouraging our students to inform their filmmaking with a deep understanding of film history and theory, and to use their production experience to inform their scholarly work. As majors, students will develop a sophisticated understanding of film history and key theoretical questions and acquire fundamental skills in screenwriting, cinematography, directing, and editing.
